ceiling_directive: Replace the separate log-propensity sieve with a coherent two-boundary log-odds sieve and establish finite, uniform information and empirical-Hessian bounds before rederiving the signed-functional, Gaussian, and subsampling expansions.
improvement_directive: Use a joint logistic-series model containing both endpoint log terms so that its score variance is weighted by π(1−π), then prove the claimed Riesz rate and oracle-transfer bounds uniformly at both boundaries. Propagate that repaired expansion through the Gaussian arm and refitted arm-vector subsampling results.
critique: The load-bearing boundary-likelihood argument is invalid on the declared class because it treats π/(1−π) as harmless although opposite-overlap controls 1−π only near the arm's zero-propensity endpoint. Even at the mixed witness, the control arm has 1−π₀(x) asymptotic to x^{3/2}/2, so its asserted information norm is infinite for spline directions nonzero near zero, contradicting the finite-variance concentration and Hessian calculations used in the proof. The same defect occurs for both arms in the two-heavy construction and leaves the signed Riesz expansion, learned-propensity Gaussian law, joint QTE law, and subsampling coverage unproved. Consequently the TL;DR and project justification stale-overclaim uniform feasible transfer and inference; what remains established consists mainly of examples, score-law bookkeeping, and conditional algebra rather than the advertised limit theory. The absence of a valid central first-stage theorem also prevents a leading-journal paper score despite the extensive formal presentation.
